subject: Holdback trigger: MAP update, Re-quote & escalation
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Rajesh Patel <rajesh@acme.com>, Acme Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Holdback trigger: MAP update, Re-quote & escalation

Rajesh / procurement team —

Quick update and a request for a short alignment call. We received the formal holdback note this morning referencing the new security review window and a procurement budget freeze for Q3. That triggers the MAP holding condition (section 3.b) and will push our planned go-live unless we agree an alternative acceptance cadence.

What we need from Acme today:
- Confirmation of the holdback scope (full platform vs. token-limited pilot).
- Procurement’s earliest available date to re-open the purchase queue (approx week).
- Any required changes to the SOW / pricing that procurement needs to release approvals.

Camila / Kim — I’m copying you to coordinate an updated MAP and a re-quote if required. If procurement will not clear funds until mid-September we should propose a staged acceptance: pilot (read-only) for early Sep + full acceptance in Oct. That keeps momentum and protects the committed credit.

I’ve attached the MAP draft that highlights acceptance milestones (MAP-v3.xlsx). We should be prepared to escalate to the account exec and ACME VP if procurement asks for additional concessions.

Proposed next step: 30-min call today at 4pm PT to confirm scope and agree a contingency cadence. Rajesh — is that possible?

Thanks,

—Jordan
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
jordan@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0139

Attachments: MAP-v3.xlsx (spreadsheet, 24KB)

From: Rajesh Patel <rajesh@acme.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Procurement <procurement@acme.com>, Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 10:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Holdback trigger: MAP update, Re-quote & escalation

Jordan —

Thanks for the heads-up. Procurement confirms a temporary hold on new platform spend for all non-compliant vendors while our security review is open. The hold is company-wide and driven by a September audit window; earliest release we can commit to right now is the week of 2026-09-20.

Scope: the hold is on full production contracts only. We can still sign limited pilot/POs that meet the security gating (data segregation + KMS in our region). I’ve attached a short procurement note with the mandatory controls.

If Redwood can accept a staged acceptance approach (pilot first, production after audit), procurement will approve a pilot PO in the next 10 business days. If not, procurement needs a final SOW + pricing that shows any changes from the current proposal.

I can make 4pm PT work for a call if we limit it to 30 minutes.

—Rajesh
Rajesh Patel
Head of IT Procurement, Acme Corp
rajesh@acme.com | +1 617-555-0222

Attachment: procurement-notes-ACME.pdf (PDF, 18KB)

From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Rajesh Patel <rajesh@acme.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 13:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Holdback trigger: MAP update, Re-quote & escalation

Rajesh — thanks for the clarity.

We’ll revise the MAP to add a staged acceptance path and a pilot PO option that explicitly lists the security checkpoints your team flagged (regional KMS, audit log retention policy, network isolation). I’ve attached a redline summary (requote-summary.docx) and updated MAP (MAP-v3.xlsx) with two timelines:

- Option A (Pilot-first): Pilot PO signed by 2026-08-25; pilot acceptance window 8/25–9/17; full production onboarding after your audit (target week of 9/20).
- Option B (Delay-to-production): Pause until audit completes; production go-live window 10/04–10/15.

Impact summary for Acme: Option A preserves start-of-eval metrics and reduces risk to revenue (delayed revenue recognition of ~30 days for production) while giving you the audit buffer. Option B pushes ARR recognition to Oct and requires a 5% one-time price holdback clause if procurement considers additional legal reviews.

Call: Jordan — let’s still take 4pm PT to align with procurement and lock the option. I’ll share a 1‑page exec brief ahead of the call.

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 13 Aug 2026 15:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Holdback trigger: MAP update, Re-quote & escalation

Kim — forwarding the thread after today’s alignment call (summary below). Need your guidance on escalation and credit authorization.

Call summary (13 Aug 2026, 4:00pm PT):
- Procurement confirms company-wide holdback; earliest release week of 2026-09-20 unless audit completes early.
- Acme will sign a pilot PO under Option A if we accept the security gate items in Procurement’s PDF.
- They asked for a documented acceptance cadence and a concise SOW change that shows the staging (pilot vs. production).
- Risk: If we require full production now, Acme will delay to Oct and ask for a pricing concession; estimated ARR impact: ~$120k deferred + potential 5% discount ask.

Asks for you:
1) Approve a pilot PO path (no credit, standard pilot terms) and authorize the SOW delta (we’ll limit scope to read-only pilot).
2) If Procurement seeks concession beyond 3% or requests credit, escalate to VP Sales — we should hold hard at 3% and prefer a staged-acceptance credit escrow instead.
3) Approve the escalation email to the ACME account exec / VP if procurement pushes for full production pricing concessions.

I’ve attached the MAP-v3 and the requote summary. If you want, I can craft the escalation note to the VP with the financial impact and recommended negotiation posture.

Thanks,

—Jordan
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
jordan@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0139
